terms.gloss: a lecture room, a hall where a discourse is heard
evidence: Quint. 2.11.3: cujus reī grātiā plēnum sit audītōrium (Lewis & Short s.v. audītōrius)
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: not in Cicero, and perhaps not before the Augustan age; Quintilian and Pliny use it of a hall for readings and lectures.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 339.
